methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $6M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
Apis Cor is a seed-stage housing and construction company that has raised $5.5M to date. The comparable universe is limited, consisting of one identifiable private peer (BotBuilt) and no public comparables, reflecting the nascent state of automated construction technology.

The valuation analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-Series A advancement. Using total capital raised ($5.5M, rounded to $6M as a proxy for implied post-money valuation) as the baseline, this method yields an implied valuation of $14M. The 2.5x multiplier reflects historical patterns in early-stage venture progression for hardware-adjacent construction plays, though the limited comp set constrains confidence in the multiple's precision for this specific subsector.

The triangulated valuation range spans $12M (low) to $16M (median $14M), derived solely from the stage-progression approach. The narrow range reflects reliance on a single applicable method rather than convergence across multiple independent approaches. Key uncertainties include the durability of stage-progression assumptions in an immature sector with one visible peer, customer traction metrics not captured in this dataset, and technology risk inherent to robotic construction systems. Additional data on Apis Cor's revenue, deployment status, and competitive positioning relative to BotBuilt would materially sharpen this analysis.
